key_insight: This paper introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark designed to test whether AI can reason about how scientific ideas evolve through lineage rather than generating ideas from scratch. It treats ideas like genomes—built from inherited mechanisms, fixes, and recombinations of prior work.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks do not measure whether AI systems can understand scientific lineage or generate ideas grounded in that lineage. This work addresses the gap between simple idea generation and the more realistic process of building on prior research.
method: Proposes the IdeaGene framework, representing each paper or proposal as a set of minimal components that capture how ideas inherit and evolve.
Builds IG-Bench to evaluate two capabilities: scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.
Organizes benchmark tasks around tracing connections between prior work, limitations, mechanisms, and proposed extensions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a more realistic way to evaluate research assistants and idea-generation systems. It can help identify models that not only produce novel-sounding proposals but can also ground them in scientific history and logical inheritance.
visual_elements: A lineage tree showing how one scientific idea branches from earlier papers.
A genome-style diagram mapping idea components to inherited mechanisms and fixes.
A benchmark pipeline illustration with inputs, reasoning steps, and generated proposals.
A comparison chart contrasting generic idea generation vs. lineage-grounded idea generation.
paper_title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
paper_authors: Yifan Zhou, Qihao Yang, Yan Li, Donggang Li, Xiru Hu
